E1.evidence: Maintainer-filed issue: "We have a broken ci-testing with the changes from https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/1913." (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/1178). The fix PR quotes the compiler errors: "controller_manager.h:141:67: error: no matching conversion for functional-style cast from 'int' to 'rclcpp::Duration'" and "gripper_controller_handle.h:152:46: error: no viable overloaded '='" (https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/pull/1181).

E2.evidence: moveit_core's controller_manager header declares "virtual bool waitForExecution(const rclcpp::Duration& timeout = rclcpp::Duration(-1)) = 0;" (moveit2 438f6d20). rclcpp PR #1913 ('remove things that were deprecated during galactic') deleted the constructor it relies on: "-  explicit Duration(rcl_duration_value_t nanoseconds);" from rclcpp/include/rclcpp/duration.hpp. The failure is a removed library API element across the boundary (not internal, not deployment wiring, not a build-system change; the consumer's source must change).

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the consumer was written against an rclcpp release that still had the constructor and was built against a newer release without it. PR #1181: "I believe this is caused by https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/1913 and rclcpp getting a new release." Issue comment: "They did a sync and now main is also broken".

E4.evidence: Build failure in CI with the compiler error quoted in PR #1181.

resolution.summary: moveit_core's default argument uses the surviving factory: "virtual bool waitForExecution(const rclcpp::Duration& timeout = rclcpp::Duration::from_nanoseconds(-1)) = 0;" (PR #1181, 14d2a932).
resolution.evidence: PR #1181 was approved and merged and closed the issue; a Codecov report exists for the PR head 515627a merged into main 438f6d2, indicating a CI build and test run, but the thread does not identify the rclcpp revision that run used, and no CI log is retrievable.

notes: Composition choice: the thread documents several compositions broken by the same rclcpp release; this spec takes moveit_core against rclcpp because the Duration error is the first one reported and the first one the fix PR addressed (the reporter then added: "I think it also fails with:" followed by the gripper_controller_handle.h:152:46 error "no viable overloaded '='"). Other compositions, not specified here, all against rclcpp_action (a separate package in the same repository) through Client::SendGoalOptions::goal_response_callback, whose compatibility wrapper accepting the old std::shared_future signature was removed by the same PR #1913: moveit_simple_controller_manager (gripper_controller_handle.h and follow_joint_trajectory_controller_handle.cpp), moveit_ros_planning_interface (move_group_interface.cpp) and moveit_hybrid_planning (hybrid_planning_manager.cpp); all fixed in the same PR #1181 by switching lambdas to the GoalHandle::SharedPtr signature. The constructor had been marked deprecated before removal (rclcpp 15.4.0 duration.hpp: "Use Duration::from_nanoseconds instead or std::chrono_literals. For example:"); no deprecation warning from moveit's builds is shown in the sources. consumer_built_against '15.4.0' is inferred: it is the last rclcpp release before 16.0.0 (bloomed into rolling 2022-04-06, rosdistro 9caccb63) and still declares the constructor, and the maintainers state main CI broke only after the sync that brought the new release. Canonical form note: the removed element is one constructor overload, so the element name carries its parameter list (api:rclcpp::Duration::Duration(rcl_duration_value_t)) to identify the overload; other Duration constructors remained. api:rclcpp::Duration::from_nanoseconds is used only by the resolved consumer revision. The inventory is limited to the header component that failed (moveit_core/controller_manager); moveit_core uses many more rclcpp symbols elsewhere.
